'''Peter Hintz''' (born 1991 in [[Kassel]], [[Germany]]) is a German mathematician working in the areas of [[partial differential equations]], [[microlocal analysis]], [[scattering theory]] and [[general relativity]]. He is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematics department welcomes new faculty for fall 2025|url=https://science.psu.edu/news/mathematics-department-welcomes-new-faculty-fall-2025|access-date=2025-10-11 |website=science.psu.edu}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Hintz graduated with a BSc in mathematics and a BSc in physics from the [[University of Göttingen]] in 2011. He obtained his PhD in 2015 at Stanford University under the supervision of [[András Vasy]].<ref>[https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=204169 Peter Hintz] in the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref>

After his postdoctoral appointments at the [[Miller Institute]] and [[Clay Mathematics Institute]], he joined the faculty of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as an assistant professor in 2019, later becoming an associate professor. In 2021, he moved to [[ETH Zürich]] as an associate professor of mathematics and physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Departures|date=July 11, 2025 |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2025/07/eight-professors-appointed.html|access-date=2025-10-11}}</ref> As of Fall 2025, he is a full professor of mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].

== Awards and honors ==

Hintz was [[Miller Institute|Miller Research Fellow]] from 2015 to 2017, where he was mentored by [[Maciej Zworski]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://miller.berkeley.edu/fellowship/awards |title=Awards: Miller Fellowship |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> He subsequently was a [[Clay Mathematics Institute|Clay Research Fellow]] from 2017 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.claymath.org/people/peter-hintz/ |title=Peter Hintz |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> During his time as a faculty member of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], he was an [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellow]] from 2020 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sloan.org/grant-detail/fg-2020-13245|title= Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship for Peter Hintz in Mathematics |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> In 2021, he delivered a plenary lecture at the 20th [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.icmp2021.com/plenary-speakers/|title= Plenary Speakers |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> The following year, Hintz gave a special invited lecture at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] together with [[:de:Gustav Holzegel|Gustav Holzegel (de)]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&order=field_speakers_congress_year&sort=asc&page=177|title= ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Hintz and Holzegel|year=2022|chapter=Recent Progress in General Relativity|title=Prize Lectures|volume=5|chapter-url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM2022/978-3-98547-559-9-volume-1.pdf}}</ref> In 2022, he was awarded the [[ETH Zürich|Golden Owl]] for excellence in teaching at ETH Zürich.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/en/the-eth-zurich/education/awards/golden-owl.html|title= Golden Owl of the VSETH |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> He received a [[Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications|Frontiers of Science Award]] in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nccr-swissmap.ch/news-and-events/news/frontiers-science-awards|title= Frontiers of Science Awards |access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> and the [[International Association of Mathematical Physics|IAMP Early Career Award]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.iamp.org/page.php?page=page_award|title=IAMP Early Career Award|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref>

== Research ==

Hintz's work applies methods from microlocal analysis as well as scattering and spectral theory to hyperbolic partial differential equations arising in Einstein's theory of [[general relativity]]. In 2026, he proved the [[black hole stability conjecture]] for the family of [[Kerr metric|Kerr black holes]] for all subextremal angular momenta.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last1=Hintz|first1=Peter|date=2026-06-26|title=Nonlinear stability of subextremal Kerr black holes|class=gr-qc|language=en|eprint=2606.28253}}</ref> Previously, in collaboration with [[András Vasy]], he proved the nonlinear stability of the [[Kerr–Newman–de–Sitter metric|Kerr-de Sitter]] family of black holes.<ref>Peter Hintz and András Vasy, [https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1560966510 "The global non-linear stability of the Kerr–de Sitter family of black holes"], Acta Mathematica 220(1), pp.&nbsp;1–206 (2018)</ref> He also co-authored a paper on possible violations of [[Roger Penrose|Sir Roger Penrose's]] [[Cosmic censorship hypothesis|strong cosmic censorship]] conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cardoso | first1=Vitor | last2=Costa | first2=João L. | last3=Destounis | first3=Kyriakos | last4=Hintz | first4=Peter | last5=Jansen | first5=Aron | title=Quasinormal Modes and Strong Cosmic Censorship | journal=Physical Review Letters | date=2018 | volume=120 | issue=3 | article-number=031103 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.031103 | pmid=29400502 | arxiv=1711.10502 | bibcode=2018PhRvL.120c1103C | url=https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.031103 }}</ref> Among his other contributions is a proof of Price's law on the rate of decay of waves on [[Kerr metric|Kerr]] black hole spacetimes.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hintz | first1=Peter | title=A Sharp Version of Price's Law for Wave Decay on Asymptotically Flat Spacetimes | journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics | date=2022 | volume=389 | issue=1 | pages=491–542 | doi=10.1007/s00220-021-04276-8 | arxiv=2004.01664 | bibcode=2022CMaPh.389..491H | hdl=20.500.11850/521855 | url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-021-04276-8 }}</ref>
